provenance.instrument: Code of the Township of East Brandywine, Chapter 399 Zoning (Zoning Ordinance of 1989, Ord. No. 89-01, as amended), with definitions in Chapter 300, as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: Chapter 399 adopted 4-27-1989 by Ord. No. 89-01. 399-91 (accessory dwellings) amended 3-17-1998, 3-27-2002, 7-21-2004 (Ord. 04-03), 3-7-2013 (Ord. 02-2013), 7-16-2014 (Ord. 02-2014, which added the by-right standards in 399-91C) and 12-20-2018 (Ord. 07-2018). The district use lists were last amended 4-16-2026 (Ord. 02-2026). Definitions moved to Chapter 300, 300-17, in 2016 (Ord. 06-2016). eCode360 New Laws (read 2026-11-13): Ord. 05-2026 (11-5-2026, a corrected zoning map scale) and Ord. 06-2026 (11-5-2026, 399-75 in an age-qualified community). Ord. 05-2026 replaces the zoning map to fix its scale. Ord. 06-2026 amends 399-75 for side and rear yards in an age-qualified community. Both were read and neither touches the accessory dwelling rules.
provenance.code_current_through_note: Latest amendment noted in the zoning use sections: Ord. No. 02-2026 (4-16-2026). Two later ordinances (05-2026 and 06-2026, 11-5-2026) are listed as New Laws, not yet codified.
checks: An 'accessory dwelling' needs a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board in R-1, R-2, R-3 and VC (399-21B(4), 399-27B(3), 399-33B(3), 399-159B(1)(b)). In TND-1 it is permitted by right (399-39A(5)). It is not listed in MU, CS/LI or I/R
Family only: at most two people, and the occupant (or one of two) must be related by blood, marriage or adoption to the owner of the house (399-91B(2), C(3))
The owner must live in the house or the unit (399-91B(3), C(4))
By special exception: inside the existing house (which may be enlarged, not into the front yard) or inside an existing accessory structure. 500 to 800 sq ft (399-91B(4), (6), (7))

A unit in the house needs a lot that meets the district's gross and net lot area for a house: R-1 3 acres gross and 55,000 sq ft net, R-2 100,000 and 45,000, R-3 1 acre and 35,000, VC 20,000 net (399-91B(5), 399-22A, 399-28A, 399-34, 399-160B)
A unit in an existing accessory structure needs at least 1.5 acres gross and 45,000 sq ft net, or the district minimum if larger (399-91B(6)(b))

By right in TND-1: only inside the existing house, never in an accessory structure. At least 500 sq ft and no maximum. New windows and doors only on the side or rear walls, no other exterior change. Public sewer required (399-91C)
No building containing a dwelling unit may be in any required yard, so a unit in an accessory structure must meet the principal building yards (399-75A)
One off-street parking space for the unit, not in a required yard. The Board may waive it. The by-right standards give no parking figure (399-91B(9), 399-108A(1))
A recorded memorandum of the Board's decision. A use and occupancy permit renewed every year, inspection at least every three years and at each change of occupant (399-91B(11), (12), C(8))

Conversion of a house that existed on 4-27-1989 into two (up to five) units is a separate path with no family rule: special exception in R-1, R-2, R-3 and VC, by right in TND-1. New units at least 950 sq ft (800 by right) (399-96)
Class I or Class II historic resources may add a two-family dwelling by conditional use in R-1, R-2, MU, CS/LI and I/R (399-67C)
A vacant nonconforming lot in single and separate ownership may be built on if the yards are met, else by special exception (399-125A)
In TND-1 the by-right standards (399-91C) set a 500 sq ft minimum and no maximum. The 800 sq ft cap shown by the tool is the special exception cap (399-91B(4)) and does not apply in TND-1
In TND-1 and VC the district lot rules apply only where adequate sewage and water are shown. Otherwise the R-3 single-family rules (1 acre) apply (399-40A, 399-160A)
Houses in a clustered residential development sit on lots smaller than the district minimum, so 399-91B(5) bars a unit inside such a house by special exception (399-21A(2), 399-33A(2))
A tenant house is a separate path on a farm of 10 acres or more in R-1, R-2 and R-3: one per property, may be newly built, no family rule (399-97G)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: East Brandywine Township. Districts (399-10A): R-1, R-2, R-3, VC, TND-1, MU, CS/LI, I/R, with overlays (floodplain, steep slope, water hazard soils, historic resources, mobile home park in R-1, TND-2 and age-qualified in R-2 and R-3). Read on eCode360 in a browser, section print views and the chapter print view searched in the page. Searched for accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, in-law, granny, ECHO, elder cottage, tenant house, carriage house, second dwelling, guest house, short-term, transient. No short-term rental rule. 399-92 allows renting rooms in the dwelling to not more than two nontransient persons.

term.note: 'A self-contained dwelling unit, resulting from the conversion of an existing single-family detached dwelling into two units, or the creation of a dwelling unit within an accessory structure, which is complete with kitchen and bath facilities ... and is physically subordinate to the primary dwelling unit that exists on the property.'

status.note: Special exception in R-1, R-2, R-3 and VC, by right in TND-1, always for a relative of the owner. The family rule limits most, so family_only, with the paths in approval.

path.note: 'Where authorized as a special exception under the terms of this chapter, accessory dwellings may be created in accordance with the following standards.' Decided by the Zoning Hearing Board under 399-145.

value.note: 'Accessory dwelling unit, in accordance with the terms of § 399-91' is a use permitted by right in TND-1. The by-right standards in 399-91C apply: inside the existing house only.

fallback_path.note: A unit that fails 399-91 (for example a tenant who is not a relative, or a new detached building) needs a variance. No unlisted-use path found.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached house into two units
value.conditions: Only a house that existed on 4-27-1989. Gross lot area 50% of the house minimum times the number of units (3 acres for two units). New unit at least 950 sq ft. No external alteration except for safety. Two spaces per unit. Up to five units. No family rule.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached house into two units
value.conditions: Only a house that existed on 4-27-1989. Gross lot area 75% of 100,000 sq ft times the number of units. New unit at least 950 sq ft. No external alteration. Two spaces per unit.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached house into two units
value.conditions: Only a house that existed on 4-27-1989. Gross lot area 100% of 1 acre times the number of units. New unit at least 950 sq ft. No external alteration. Two spaces per unit.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached house into two units
value.conditions: Only a house that existed on 4-27-1989. New unit at least 950 sq ft. No external alteration. Two spaces per unit.
value.note: 399-96B(3) gives lot area multipliers only for R-1, R-2 and R-3.

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached house into two units
value.conditions: Only a house that existed on 4-27-1989. Gross lot area 50% of the house minimum times the number of units. New unit at least 800 sq ft. No external alteration. One space per unit. Public sewer.
value.note: TND-1 sets a 5,000 sq ft net lot, read here as the house minimum.

value.name: Two-family dwelling
value.conditions: Permitted use in TND-1. A net lot area of 3,500 sq ft per dwelling unit (7,000 for two), width 40 ft, front 5 to 12 ft build-to, side 7.5 ft, rear 25 ft. No family rule.

value.name: Tenant house on a farm of 10 acres or more
value.conditions: On a property used for agriculture that is 10 acres or more, one tenant house in addition to the main house. One per property. It may be newly built where no second dwelling existed on the effective date. Sited so the tenant house could later be subdivided onto its own lot. No family or employee rule in the text. Agriculture is a permitted use in R-1, R-2 and R-3.
value.note: The property must be in agricultural use. Ask the township what counts.

value.name: Two-family dwelling on a Class I or Class II historic resource
value.conditions: Only on a property designated Class I or Class II on the Historic Resources Map, approved by the Board of Supervisors when the historic structure will be preserved. One principal use per structure.

alternatives.note: Not ADUs. The conversion has no family rule.

building_types.note: 'within existing single-family detached dwellings or authorized existing accessory structures'.

existing_structure_only.note: The house may be expanded to hold the unit (B(7)(a)), so an addition is allowed by special exception. A unit outside the house must be in an existing accessory structure (see gates).

historic_bypass.note: The historic incentives add other uses by conditional use. They do not change 399-91.

requires_conforming_lot.note: By special exception a unit in the house needs the district's gross and net lot area for a house. Shown by district in gates. The by-right standards in TND-1 have no lot rule.

value.condition: The unit needs the R-1 lot area for a house: 3 acres gross and 55,000 sq ft net. This holds for a unit in the house and, being larger than 1.5 acres, for one in an accessory structure.
The unit needs the R-2 lot area for a house: 100,000 sq ft gross and 45,000 sq ft net. This holds for a unit in the house and, being larger than 1.5 acres, for one in an accessory structure.
A unit inside the house needs the R-3 lot area for a house: 1 acre gross and 35,000 sq ft net.
A unit inside the house needs the VC lot area: 20,000 sq ft net.
A unit in an accessory structure needs at least 1.5 acres gross and 45,000 sq ft net, or the district minimum if larger.
A unit outside the house must be in an accessory structure that already exists on the lot with the house.

In TND-1 (by right) the unit must be inside the existing house and not in an accessory structure. Windows and doors may be added only on the side or rear walls. No other exterior change. Public sewer required.
No enlargement of the house for the unit may be in a front yard. No exterior change out of character with the neighborhood. Architectural plans and proof of structural soundness.
Connect to a community sewage system where one is available. Otherwise a Chester County Health Department permit showing the on-site system is adequate.
A memorandum of the Board's decision is recorded as a covenant. A use and occupancy permit is renewed every year, with inspection at least every three years and at each new occupant.
A vacant nonconforming lot in single and separate ownership may be built on if the yards are met. Otherwise a special exception, not granted below 50% of the district lot area or width.

types_allowed.note: By special exception: in the house, in an enlargement of it (B(7)(a)), or in an existing accessory structure. No new detached building. In TND-1 only inside the house (see gates).

value.garage_conversion: Unit inside an existing garage or other accessory structure
value.over_garage: Unit on an upper floor of an existing accessory structure
value.attached: Unit in an enlargement of the house

max_sqft.note: 'The floor area of an accessory dwelling unit shall not be less than 500 square feet and shall not be more than 800 square feet.' The by-right standards in TND-1 set only the 500 sq ft minimum (C(5)).

internal_uses_district_height.note: A unit in the house takes the district height (3 stories or 35 ft in R-1, R-2, R-3 and VC).

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'No principal building and no other building containing a dwelling unit or other habitable living space shall be erected within or shall project into any required yard in any district.'

max_height_ft.note: No height rule for a garage or other accessory building. Garden sheds may be 12 ft. The district height applies.

owner_occupancy.note: 'One of the two dwelling units shall be occupied by the owner of the lot on which both proposed dwelling units are to be located.'

family_only.note: 'A single occupant or, in the case of two occupants, one of the two, must be related by blood, marriage, or adoption to the owner of the principal residence.'

occupancy.value: At most two people. The occupant, or one of two, is related by blood, marriage or adoption to the owner of the house.

max_adus.note: 'There shall not be more than one accessory dwelling unit created on any single-family residential lot.'

sale_apart_allowed.note: Not addressed in 399-91. Chapter 300 says an accessory structure may not become an additional principal structure.

short_term_rental_banned.note: No short-term rental rule. The family rule limits who may live in the unit.

spaces_required.note: 'One off-street parking space shall be required for the accessory dwelling unit, in addition to those utilized by the principal dwelling.' Not in a required yard. The Board may waive it. The by-right standards (C) give no figure.

total_on_site.note: By special exception: the house's two spaces plus one. In TND-1 see parking.reading.

reading.value: Special exception: one more space, three in all (399-91B(9)). By right in TND-1: 399-91C sets no parking figure, so 399-108A(1) ('single-family and two-family dwellings: two parking spaces for each dwelling unit') may ask two for the unit, four in all. Ask the zoning officer.

new_connection_required.note: The unit is served by the community sewage system where available (always in TND-1). No separate connection rule.

min_lot_sqft.note: 3 acres gross, 55,000 sq ft net. Width 200 ft.

setback_side_ft.note: Principal buildings 50 ft from any side or rear line.

min_lot_sqft.note: 100,000 sq ft gross, 45,000 net. Width 175 ft.
1 acre gross, 35,000 sq ft net. Width 150 ft.

setback_side_ft.note: Two side yards totaling 60 ft, neither under 20 ft.

min_lot_sqft.note: Net. 10,000 per use in a combination. Width 100 ft.

setback_side_ft.note: None where buildings share a party wall.

principal_max_height_ft.note: Four stories or 45 ft. At most 15% of the footprint above 3 stories or 35 ft.
